edits.text: Correlating two clinical event tables for a patient requires joining each through admissions on subject_id and comparing charttimes so the earlier event precedes the later; sharing a month alone implies no ordering.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL joins procedures_icd and diagnoses_icd to admissions to get subject_id, then filters T1.charttime < T2.charttime alongside a start-of-month equality.

edits.text: Top-N 'most common' answers use DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) with rank <= N, returning descriptive long_title names instead of raw codes, so tied ranks may yield more than N rows.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL groups by icd_code, applies DENSE_RANK on counts, filters rank <= 4, and finally selects d_icd_diagnoses.long_title.

edits.text: Year-scoped filters compare datetime(col,'start of year') against the anchor timestamp's start of year rather than using strftime('%Y') string equality, which mishandles anchoring.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL filters both event tables with datetime(charttime,'start of year') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','start of year','-0 year').

edits.text: Two clinical records belong to the same hospital visit only when their hadm_id match; matching subject_id alone pairs events from different admissions.
edits.evidence: the correct SQL correlates diagnoses with ON T1.subject_id = T2.subject_id AND T1.hadm_id = T2.hadm_id

edits.text: Match clinical concepts by name resolved through dictionary tables (e.g. d_icd_diagnoses.long_title) to look up the code, never hardcoding icd_code literals.
edits.evidence: icd_code = ( SELECT d_icd_diagnoses.icd_code FROM d_icd_diagnoses WHERE long_title = 'diarrhea' )

edits.text: 'After'/'before' between two events means strictly later/earlier charttime via < or >, not <=, so co-timed records in the same visit are excluded.
edits.evidence: the ordering predicate is T1.charttime < T2.charttime

edits.text: Yes/no questions phrased 'Has/Does/Is there any...' return a single boolean via SELECT COUNT(*)>0, not the matching rows, timestamps or labels themselves.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL is SELECT COUNT(*)>0 FROM labevents WHERE ... instead of SELECT labevents.charttime, d_labitems.label ...

edits.text: Patient-to-event filters route through the visits table: event.hadm_id IN (SELECT hadm_id FROM admissions WHERE subject_id = ?), rather than filtering event.subject_id directly.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL uses labevents.hadm_id IN (SELECT admissions.hadm_id FROM admissions WHERE admissions.subject_id = 10020786).

edits.text: Year-scoped filters use datetime(col,'start of year') compared with the anchor, not strftime('%Y'), and must also be applied to every other event table in the query, not only the anchor event.
edits.evidence: The labevents subquery repeats datetime(labevents.charttime,'start of year') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','start of year','-0 year') instead of only filtering the procedure event.

edits.text: Group and rank 'most common' answers by the dictionary code (itemid, icd_code), not by label; labels aren't unique, so resolve names only in the outermost query.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL does GROUP BY T2.itemid and joins back WHERE d_labitems.itemid IN (...), whereas grouping on d_labitems.label merges distinct items.

edits.text: 'First'/'last' an item was received means the record(s) at the extreme timestamp: match charttime = (SELECT MIN/MAX charttime ...), never ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1, so ties at that instant all return.
edits.evidence: diagnoses_icd.charttime = ( SELECT DISTINCT diagnoses_icd.charttime FROM diagnoses_icd ... ORDER BY diagnoses_icd.charttime ASC LIMIT 1 )

edits.text: 'Which/what name' answers return DISTINCT descriptive names, since the same long_title recurs across codes or visits and would otherwise repeat in results.
edits.evidence: SELECT DISTINCT d_icd_diagnoses.long_title FROM d_icd_diagnoses

edits.text: Patient-to-event filters route through hadm_id, and ICU event tables (chartevents, inputevents, outputevents) additionally through stay_id: event.stay_id IN (SELECT stay_id FROM icustays WHERE hadm_id IN ...); never filter an event table's own subject_id column.
edits.evidence: WHERE chartevents.stay_id IN (SELECT icustays.stay_id FROM icustays WHERE icustays.hadm_id IN (SELECT admissions.hadm_id FROM admissions WHERE subject_id = 10003046))

edits.text: Day- or period-bucketed measurements return one row per bucket holding only the aggregated value; the date expression belongs in GROUP BY, not in the SELECT list.
edits.evidence: SELECT MAX(chartevents.valuenum) FROM chartevents ... GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m-%d',chartevents.charttime)

edits.text: Questions relating a follow-up event to an earlier one pair the two event types on subject_id across all visits, not hadm_id; the follow-up may belong to a later admission.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL joins T1 (procedures_icd+admissions) to T2 (labevents+admissions) ON T1.subject_id = T2.subject_id, whereas the agent paired labs to the procedure's hadm_id.

edits.text: Match clinical concepts through the dictionary for that event type - d_icd_procedures/d_icd_diagnoses.long_title, d_items/d_labitems.label - never hardcode icd_code or itemid literals.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL resolves the procedure code via d_icd_procedures.long_title = '...'; the agent hardcoded an icd_code literal.

edits.text: Relating a follow-up drug or event to an earlier one pairs records on subject_id across admissions; add hadm_id equality only when the question says 'same hospital visit'.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL joins T1 and T2 ON T1.subject_id = T2.subject_id with WHERE T1.hadm_id = T2.hadm_id, so both drugs must fall in one admission.

edits.text: For 'N most common' answers rank groups by COUNT(*) with DENSE_RANK and keep rank <= N, never LIMIT N, returning the grouped value not its count; ties may add rows beyond N.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL wraps the GROUP BY in DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) then WHERE C1 <= 3 and selects only T3.drug, instead of ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 3.

edits.text: Choosing the 'first' (or last) hospital visit or ICU stay excludes ongoing ones: require dischtime IS NOT NULL (or outtime IS NOT NULL) before ORDER BY admittime/intime LIMIT 1.
edits.evidence: FROM admissions WHERE subject_id = 10038999 AND admissions.dischtime IS NOT NULL ORDER BY admissions.admittime ASC LIMIT 1, mirroring the examples' icustays.outtime IS NOT NULL filter.

edits.text: 'Last year'/'this year' are calendar years, not rolling windows: compare datetime(col,'start of year') to datetime(anchor,'start of year','-1 year'), applying this to every event table in the query.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL filters datetime(admissions.admittime,'start of year') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','start of year','-1 year'), not the agent's datetime(admittime) >= datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','-1 year') rolling-year test.

edits.text: A named month inside 'this year' keeps the year-scope equality and adds strftime('%m', col) = 'NN'; that is a component match, not a shifted anchor such as start of month.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL keeps datetime(labevents.charttime,'start of year') = datetime(...,'start of year','-0 year') and adds AND strftime('%m',labevents.charttime) = '11'; the agent substituted 'start of month' for the anchor and dropped the year check.

edits.text: Two records of the same event type compared within one visit are two filtered copies joined on subject_id AND hadm_id, ordered by each copy's own charttime.
edits.evidence: T1 and T2 are both diagnoses_icd subqueries joined ON T1.subject_id = T2.subject_id AND T1.hadm_id = T2.hadm_id with WHERE T1.charttime < T2.charttime.

edits.text: A year or period scope binds each record's own charttime, not the admission's admittime, and must be repeated on every filtered copy of an event table.
edits.evidence: Both T1 and T2 filter strftime('%Y',diagnoses_icd.charttime) = '2100' rather than admissions.admittime.

edits.text: 'How many patients' counts COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) over the qualifying rows, so a patient with several matching visits is counted once.
edits.evidence: SELECT COUNT( DISTINCT T1.subject_id )

edits.text: A 'within N months following' relation between a procedure and a later prescription matches on subject_id, not hadm_id, so the pair may span two different hospital visits.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL joins T1 (procedures+admissions) to T2 (prescriptions+admissions) ON T1.subject_id = T2.subject_id with no hadm_id equality.

edits.text: Drug values are pre-normalized lowercase strings; match a named drug by exact equality, not LIKE or case-insensitive patterns that could pull sibling formulations.
edits.evidence: Correct SQL uses WHERE prescriptions.drug = 'acetaminophen', whereas the agent used p.drug LIKE '%acetaminophen%'.

edits.text: Relative period words map to calendar-year equality against the literal now: 'previous year'/'last year' is datetime(col,'start of year') = datetime(now,'start of year','-1 year').
edits.evidence: datetime(procedures_icd.charttime,'start of year') = datetime('2100-12-31 23:59:00','start of year','-1 year') and the identical test on prescriptions.starttime
